Found it, and no Mac was needed. Lane session-messaging-plan read the Claude Code 2.1.319 program itself. The limit is a built-in guard in Claude Code, not our code. Each message between sessions carries a list of the sessions it has passed through. Once a session appears 10 times in that list, Claude Code drops the message as a loop. A back-and-forth between two sessions adds one entry each round, so the talk stops after about 10 rounds. A message you type yourself starts a fresh list, which is why your word resets it. The limit comes from a setting on Anthropic's servers, and we found no setting you can change. Step session-messaging-plan will design around it.

Update 21:38 CST Nov 7: session-messaging-plan is in progress in its own lane. Source: the roadmap. Triage.
